moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.0: Construction: place the matching controller and connect real Create power to its rear shaft. Open the front panel. Choose the exact car configuration, a 16/32/48 block bed, its world origin and cardinal direction. Preview spends nothing. Cyan outlines show the full moving structure sweep; gold outlines show fixed machinery; green boxes identify native dock anchors. Socket positions lists exact block coordinates. Close the panel to place native anchors while nearby preview ghosts remain visible; Clear preview removes them. Clear the sweep and validate. Build then consumes the server-listed parts and functional insert modules. After Build, use the normal matching track tool to connect fixed approach rails to the exact sockets; Capture refuses until they are valid. Existing curves on a shifted or angled socket must be removed and rejoined after Build. Keep the controller outside the sweep and within eight blocks when operating.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.1: Parts and survival: craft bed beams, overhead gantries or Pipeline side-contact beds, guides, pivots, end locks and docking sockets. Each has its own recipe. The matching controller uses a precision mechanism and the relevant Create drive component. Craft the exact family insert with its normal track item plus eight iron ingots: eight modules per recipe, one module per bed-length block. Skins, colors and car body variants never grant mechanical compatibility. The panel shows the exact structural bill before Build.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.2: Operating and recovery: board at a fixed station, close restraints and stop the complete train on the bed. Capture retains all chassis and carriers. Choose a destination, then Move. Release requires the real bed to stop and align, locks to engage and the exact receiving rail to be reserved and reconnected. Power loss, obstruction, broken support, unload and restart hold the train. Inspect the cause and use explicit Resume or Return; no saved release flag grants permission. Evacuation requires stationary retained bodies and safe measured exits. Never board, couple or repaint while retained.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.3: Wing transfer example: choose Wing, length 16 and translation 4. With origin (0,80,0) facing south, the starting rail anchors are (0,80,-8) and (0,80,8); the second span is four blocks east. Place matching original native approach rails. Preview and build the visible bed, outboard guides and locks. Board one Wing car at a fixed station, stop it wholly within the bed, close restraints, Capture, Move to end, then Release only after measured locking.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.4: Wing turntable example: choose Wing, length 16, ports 0° to 90°. Preview marks the two perpendicular fixed spans around the same center. Build each approach with the normal track tool; keep the full circular sweep clear. The full-show option performs an extra bounded turn before the same named exit. Never use a visual heading alone as docking evidence: the panel’s measured locks and release guards remain authoritative.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.5: Dive drop example: choose Dive, length 16 and drop 4. Install Dive inserts and matching native Dive approach rails at the upper and lower sockets. Clear the vertical sweep below all six seats. The downward stroke is bounded, not free fall; the reset is powered. Capture the complete stopped car, Move to the lower dock, Release after locking, then return the empty bed explicitly.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.6: Wing tilt example: choose Wing and 30° or 90° tilt. The bed pivots at its center. Exact angled socket positions are computed from the finite program; never round the rail endpoint geometry to a block grid. The visible native anchor identifies the socket while the native rail attaches at its exact endpoint. Keep the full pitched train and rider sweep clear. Classic Spinning may use only the 30° option.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.7: Classic Spinning elevator example: choose Classic Spinning S1, length 16 and lift 4, 8, 16 or 32. Use S1 inserts, a real elevated receiving span and full-height guides. Close restraints and latch the local spinning carrier before capture. This level lift does not grant S1 inverted/90° tilt capability. A stopped lift with lost power remains held until an explicit recovery request passes inspection.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.8: Wing teeter example: choose Wing, length 16 and one to three cycles. Build one starting dock and clear the complete ±15° pitch sweep. Capture only a stopped complete train. The finite show returns to its original level pose; Release still waits for measured locks. Do not place approach scenery, riders or machinery inside the teeter envelope.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.9: S2 side-drop example: choose S2, length 16 and side-drop 4 or 8. The bed stays level while translating diagonally down and sideways by the selected amount. Preview locates the second fixed span and the combined sweep. Retain the spinning carrier before capture. Build the second real receiving track before movement; this is not a teleport between disconnected anchors.
moving.fourthdimension.guide.page.10: S2 compound and alternate mount examples: compound combines the shortest yaw turn (at most 180°) with +15° or -15° pitch and finishes level at the selected port. Use the full simultaneous sweep. For suspended families choose an overhead gantry, leaving the under-rail rider space open. For Pipeline choose its distinct low side-contact bed. Compatibility lists all 22 configurations and limits; only original supported pairings can be built.
